source: NOAA Office for Coastal Management, R-Factor for the Conterminous United States (800 m GeoTIFF, 2013), from the isoerodent maps in USDA Agriculture Handbook 703 (Renard et al., 1997)
credit: R values: NOAA Office for Coastal Management and Renard et al. (1997), AH 703. County and state lines: U.S. Census Bureau. Map frame: K-State USLE workbook.
about: The R factor (rainfall and runoff) is the erosive power of rainfall in an average year, the sum of storm energy times maximum 30-minute intensity. These values come from the national isoerodent (equal-R) map in Agriculture Handbook 703, interpolated smoothly between the map's lines, so R changes gradually across Kansas: about 75 in the far west to about 250 in the southeast.
instructions: Click your site on the map, enter its coordinates, or use your device's location. You can also type an R value.
